questions.prompt: Which instrument would a biologist use to measure the temperature of water in a pond they are studying?
questions.explanation: A thermometer measures temperature. A balance measures mass, a measuring cylinder measures volume, and a microscope makes small things look bigger.

questions.prompt: Why should a scientist write down the results of an experiment as soon as they are measured?
options: So the data are accurate and not forgotten or changed
To make the report look longer
questions.explanation: Recording results straight away keeps the data accurate and trustworthy, because relying on memory can lead to mistakes or forgotten readings.

questions.prompt: Which part of a cell is a tiny structure where the energy of cellular respiration is released?
questions.explanation: The mitochondrion is the site where energy is released from glucose during cellular respiration. It is often called the powerhouse of the cell.

questions.prompt: Which body system gives the body its shape and supports it so a person can stand upright?
questions.explanation: The skeletal system (the bones) supports the body, gives it shape, and protects organs. The other systems carry out different jobs.

questions.prompt: Which group of micro-organisms causes the skin disease ringworm and the spoiling of damp bread?
questions.explanation: Fungi, such as moulds, cause ringworm of the skin and spoil damp bread. The name ringworm is misleading because it is a fungus, not a worm.

questions.prompt: The huge variety of different living things found in an area is called its:
questions.explanation: Biodiversity means the variety of different living things in an area. A population is just one kind of organism in one place.

questions.prompt: A scientist tests whether a fertiliser helps teff grow. One group of plants gets fertiliser; another identical group gets none. Why is the group with no fertiliser used?
options: To compare against, and show the fertiliser is the cause of any difference
Because teff does not need fertiliser
questions.explanation: The untreated group is a control. Comparing it with the treated group shows whether the fertiliser, and not something else, caused any change in growth.

questions.prompt: A nerve cell is long and thin with branched ends. How does this shape help it do its job?
options: It lets the cell make its own food
It stores large amounts of water
It helps the cell carry messages quickly over long distances
It allows the cell to swim
questions.explanation: A nerve cell's long, branched shape lets it carry electrical messages rapidly from one part of the body to another. Its structure suits its function.

questions.prompt: The cell membrane is described as partially (selectively) permeable. This means it:
options: Lets every substance pass through freely
Lets some substances pass but blocks others
questions.explanation: A partially permeable membrane allows some substances (such as water and small molecules) to pass while controlling or blocking others. This lets the cell manage its contents.

questions.prompt: Many similar cells working together form a tissue. What is formed when several different tissues work together for one main job?
questions.explanation: An organ, such as the heart or stomach, is made of several different tissues that work together to carry out a particular function.

questions.prompt: Bile breaks large drops of fat into many tiny droplets during digestion. Why does this help?
options: It turns the fat into protein
It gives a larger surface for enzymes to act on the fat
questions.explanation: Breaking fat into tiny droplets greatly increases the surface area, so fat-digesting enzymes can work on it faster. Bile does not digest fat itself.

questions.prompt: When a person cuts their finger, the bleeding usually stops after a short time. This is mainly because the blood:
options: Forms a clot that seals the wound
Stops being made by the heart
questions.explanation: Blood forms a clot at a wound, sealing it to stop further bleeding and to keep out germs while the skin heals.

questions.prompt: Milk is often heated strongly for a short time before it is sold. The main reason for this is to:
options: Kill harmful micro-organisms so the milk is safer
questions.explanation: Heating milk kills most harmful micro-organisms, making it safer to drink and helping it keep longer. This process is called pasteurisation.

questions.prompt: Tears and the acid in the stomach both help protect the body because they:
options: Kill or remove many germs before they cause disease
questions.explanation: Tears wash germs from the eyes and contain germ-killing substances, while stomach acid kills many germs in swallowed food. Both are natural defences against disease.

questions.prompt: When using a key to identify a living thing, each step offers two choices. What kind of question gives only two possible answers at each step?
options: An open question with many answers
A question with a yes or no (either/or) answer
questions.explanation: A key works by asking either/or (yes or no) questions. Each answer leads to the next step until the organism is identified.

questions.prompt: Lions and leopards are closely related and share many features. In classification they would most likely belong to the same:
questions.explanation: Closely related organisms that share many features are grouped into the same genus. They are still different species, so they are not the same species.

questions.prompt: In a grassland, there are very many grass plants, fewer grasshoppers, and only a few birds that eat the grasshoppers. The number of living things usually:
options: Has nothing to do with feeding
questions.explanation: The number of organisms usually decreases along a food chain, because energy is lost at each step, so fewer organisms can be supported at higher levels.

questions.prompt: Some birds fly to a different region when the dry season comes and food becomes scarce. This movement to survive is best described as:
questions.explanation: Migration is the movement of animals to another area to find food, water, or better conditions, helping them survive when resources run low.

questions.prompt: Two students measure the same leaf and get 6 cm and 9 cm. The best way to get a more reliable result is to:
options: Take several measurements and find the average
Guess a value in between without measuring
questions.explanation: Taking several careful measurements and averaging them reduces the effect of individual mistakes and gives a more reliable result than choosing one reading.

questions.prompt: A young enset plant grows much larger over several months. At the cell level, this growth happens mainly because:
options: Existing cells get heavier without changing
Cells divide to make more cells, which then enlarge
The plant takes in ready-made cells from the soil
questions.explanation: Growth happens as cells divide to form new cells, which then grow larger. The plant does not absorb whole cells from the soil.

questions.prompt: On a hot day a plant that has not been watered begins to droop. Using osmosis, the best explanation is that the cells have:
options: Gained water and become too firm
Lost water, so they are no longer firm enough to hold the plant up
Filled with air from the soil
questions.explanation: When the plant loses more water than it takes in, the cells lose water by osmosis and become flaccid (soft), so they can no longer keep the plant firm and it droops.

questions.prompt: After sprinting, a person keeps breathing fast and deep for a while even though they have stopped running. The most likely reason is to:
options: Take in extra oxygen the muscles needed but could not get during the sprint
Make new red blood cells immediately
questions.explanation: During hard exercise the muscles cannot get enough oxygen, so the body keeps breathing deeply afterwards to supply the extra oxygen that the muscles still need.

questions.prompt: Blood passes through the human heart twice for each complete trip around the body: once to the lungs and once to the rest of the body. The main advantage of this is that:
options: The heart can stop more often
Blood is pumped at higher pressure to the body, so it travels quickly
questions.explanation: Returning to the heart after the lungs lets the blood be pumped again at high pressure to the body. This keeps oxygen-rich blood moving quickly to all the cells.

questions.prompt: Why are patients told to finish the full course of antibiotics, even if they feel better early?
options: So the medicine does not go to waste
So all the bacteria are killed and resistant ones are less likely to survive and spread
questions.explanation: Stopping early can leave some of the stronger bacteria alive. These may survive and multiply, leading to bacteria that the antibiotic can no longer kill (resistance).

questions.prompt: A child is vaccinated against measles but later catches a different disease. This is most likely because:
options: A vaccine usually protects only against the one disease it is made for
questions.explanation: A vaccine trains the body to fight one particular disease. It does not protect against unrelated diseases, so a measles vaccine cannot prevent a different illness.

questions.prompt: An animal is called by three different local names in three regions of Ethiopia. Why does giving it one agreed scientific name help science?
options: Scientists everywhere then know exactly which organism is meant
It puts the animal in a new kingdom
questions.explanation: A single scientific name removes confusion from many local names, so scientists in different places can be sure they are all talking about the same organism.

questions.prompt: Two organisms are found to share many detailed features and are placed in the same small group. Scientists conclude that the two organisms are probably:
options: Closely related and share a common ancestor
questions.explanation: Sharing many features suggests organisms are closely related and descended from a common ancestor. The more features shared, the closer the relationship is thought to be.

questions.prompt: Two plant species grow in the same small plot and both need the same light, water, and space. The relationship between them is best described as:
questions.explanation: When organisms need the same limited resources, they compete for them. Competition can affect how well each species grows and survives in that area.

questions.prompt: In a food web, hyenas eat many smaller animals. If all the hyenas were removed, what is the most likely first effect?
options: The smaller animals they ate would die out at once
The Sun would stop giving energy
The numbers of the smaller animals they ate would rise
questions.explanation: Removing a predator usually allows its prey to increase in number, at least at first, because fewer of them are being eaten. This can then affect other parts of the web.

questions.prompt: Decomposers return nitrogen-containing substances to the soil. Why is this important for plants?
options: Plants use these substances to make proteins for growth
Plants drink them instead of water
questions.explanation: Plants take up nitrogen compounds from the soil and use them to build proteins, which are needed for healthy growth. Recycling by decomposers keeps this supply going.

questions.prompt: A student wants to find out if light affects how fast a plant grows. To make it a fair test, the student should keep the same for both plants everything EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: In a fair test only the factor being studied is changed. Here that is the amount of light, while water, soil, and pot size are kept the same for both plants.

questions.prompt: Under a microscope, a cell is seen to have a cell wall but NO chloroplasts and no large central vacuole that traps light. The cell most likely comes from:
options: A root deep in the soil
questions.explanation: A plant cell with a cell wall but no chloroplasts is likely from a part that gets no light, such as a root. Animal cells have no cell wall at all.

questions.prompt: A person's gums bleed and wounds heal slowly. A doctor suspects a shortage of which dietary substance, often found in fruits and vegetables?
questions.explanation: A shortage of vitamin C causes bleeding gums and slow healing (a condition called scurvy). Fruits and vegetables are good sources of vitamin C.

questions.prompt: A village suffers from a disease spread by drinking dirty river water. Which single action would most directly reduce this disease?
options: Boiling or treating drinking water before use
questions.explanation: The disease is water-borne, so making the drinking water safe by boiling or treating it tackles the cause directly. Mosquito nets help against insect-borne diseases instead.

questions.prompt: An organism is single-celled, lives in pond water, has a true nucleus, and moves by changing its shape. Into which kingdom is it best placed?
questions.explanation: A single-celled organism with a true nucleus that lives in water (such as Amoeba) belongs to Protista. Monera have no true nucleus, and plants and animals are many-celled.

questions.prompt: In the food chain grass to insects to small birds, a disease suddenly kills most of the insects. What is the most likely effect on the small birds and the grass?
questions.explanation: With fewer insects to eat, the birds have less food and decrease in number. With fewer insects eating it, the grass is likely to increase.
